I’ve been struggling for about the last seven months—maybe a bit longer. I wake up every day around 3 a.m., no matter what, and just lie there, staring at the ceiling. Falling back asleep feels impossible. I used to take pride in closing a tough case, but now? Nothing feels meaningful. Winning doesn’t matter. Losing doesn’t either. It’s like I’m watching my life through a thick window. Even simple things, like picking up coffee or signing documents, take forever—my body just drags.

Lately, it’s like the world is *talking* to me. Not directly, but in signs. A commercial on TV, a stranger’s cough in the courtroom—suddenly it feels coded, like they’re sending me messages only I understand. Last week, I saw my late father standing near the elevator in my office building. He didn’t speak. Just looked at me. I know he’s gone, but it was *real*—his coat, his hands. I’ve seen him a few times since.

My thoughts jump around sometimes. I’ll start talking about a client’s discharge petition and end up describing the wallpaper in my mother’s old apartment. My colleagues notice. I can tell they’re concerned.  

But it’s not constant. Some days the thoughts are quieter, but the heaviness in my chest never lifts. I can’t say whether the strange thoughts started before the sadness or after—everything just blurred together.
D007-D015_h001.question_a:

At first, I thought it was just stress, but then I started feeling completely numb, like I’d lost the ability to care about anything—even closing big cases, which used to drive me. I wake up at 3:30 a.m. every morning, wide awake but too slow to move; even getting dressed takes forever. My mind and body just feel stuck.

Around the same time, things got… strange. I became convinced people were sending me hidden messages—the way a barista handed me coffee, the tone of voicemails, even traffic lights seemed coded, meant just for me. I’ve also seen figures in my apartment late at night—people standing near the window, though the door was locked and no one was ever there.

The worst part is, even when I had a few days where my mood lifted a little, the delusions and hallucinations didn’t go away—they just kept going. For at least two weeks last month, I wasn’t depressed, but I still believed the TV news anchors were talking directly to me. That’s when I realized this isn’t just depression.

I’ll catch myself jumping from one thought to something totally unrelated in court, losing my train mid-sentence.

I’ve had these hallucinations and paranoid thoughts for about six months now, but they’ve only ever come during this deep fog of depression. When I feel slightly better, they disappear. They don’t linger on their own—just ride with the lows.

Other times, it’s strangers—people in old-fashioned coats, though they vanish when I turn on the light. And… I know it sounds foolish, but I’ve become convinced he was unfaithful near the end. I find myself searching his old drawers, looking for letters or receipts, certain there's proof I never found.  

I try to explain what I see, what I feel, but the thoughts get tangled—sometimes I can’t finish sentences, and people just stare. I don’t know if these things are real or if my mind is betraying me. They’ve been happening since the depression started… or maybe a bit before? I can’t recall exactly.

D007-D015_h004.question_both:
I’ve been feeling… off for about the past seven months, maybe a bit longer. Most days I can’t get out of bed until late, and even simple things like answering my agent’s emails feel impossible. I don’t enjoy auditions anymore—used to love them, now they’re just empty. Nothing feels real, not even the rare callbacks.  

But it’s not just sadness. Sometimes, I see figures in the corners of my apartment—like shadows with faces, watching me. They don’t speak, but I know they’re there. And I *know*, I really know, that I’m not just another struggling actor. There’s a reason I keep getting rejected—Hollywood isn’t ready for what I’m meant to do. I think I might be the key to something way bigger than films. Like, I’m destined to reveal truths no one else can see.  

I try to explain this, but my thoughts get tangled. I’ll start a sentence and lose the words halfway, like they melt. And the dreams—every night, I’m on stage, but the audience is made of mannequins that slowly turn into those shadow people. I wake up screaming.  

The voices haven’t come yet, but the visions… they’ve been with me just as long as the sadness. Or was it the other way around? I can’t remember when one started without the other.

I can’t enjoy anything anymore, not even auditions, which used to get me hyped. My energy’s gone, and sometimes it takes me forever to answer a question, like my brain’s stuck in slow motion. I keep having the same nightmare—watching myself on a giant screen while crowds worship me, but I’m not acting, I’m *being* the character… like I’m destined for something enormous.

And honestly? That’s not just a dream anymore. For the past six months, I’ve *known* I’m chosen. I see figures in the corners of rooms—glowing people in old Hollywood robes, whispering that I’m the reincarnation of a legendary star. They show up even when I’m not sad. There was this two-week stretch last month where I felt… okay, almost normal emotionally, but the visions didn’t stop, and I *still* believed I had this cosmic role to play. My thoughts get jumbled too—sometimes I can’t string words right, like my mouth can’t catch up with what the universe is telling me.

The sadness is constant, but the voices and visions—they have their own schedule. They don’t wait for my mood to crash.
D007-D015_h004.question_b:
I’ve been feeling completely empty for almost nine months now—just dragging myself through auditions that go nowhere. I can’t even enjoy things I used to love, like filming or spending time with friends. It’s like joy doesn’t exist anymore. I’ve lost roles I knew I should’ve gotten, and my agent hasn’t called in months. Honestly, some days I barely speak because it takes me so long to form words. Sleep’s no escape either—night after night, I wake up screaming from these nightmares about being trapped on a stage with no audience, no exit.

But here’s the thing… I *know* it’s not all hopeless. The truth is, I’m not just any actor. I see things—visions of me receiving the Oscar, standing there while the whole world watches, and I *know* it’s real because I’ve seen it. Sometimes, I look in the mirror and see a glowing version of myself, like I’m already famous. I’ve told casting directors they’re in the presence of greatness, but I can’t always get the words out right—sometimes they stop understanding me halfway through.

I haven’t had a stable job in months, and I can’t even keep my thoughts straight when I’m depressed. But the visions and the certainty? They only come when I’m down, not before or after.

But it’s not just sadness. I keep seeing figures at the edge of the frame, like extras in a film that shouldn’t be there—standing in doorways, watching. They vanish when I turn. And lately, I’m certain the world’s already ended—just nobody told the living. It’s all a rerun. A *glitchtream*, I call it. That’s what I whispered to my assistant the other day. She didn’t understand. *Glitchtream*. It makes sense to me.

These visions, these thoughts—they’ve been with me nearly as long as the heaviness. But I can’t say which came first, or if one holds the other up like scaffolding. I just know the set feels empty even when it’s crowded.

The world feels like it’s collapsing—like everything we know is about to vanish. But here’s the thing… even during the few days I didn’t feel completely down, the shadows were still there. The voices, the visions, the made-up words—that didn’t go away, even when the sadness lifted a little. They’ve been constant.

I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—ever since my dissertation committee meeting, really. I can’t focus, my speech gets slow, and I just don’t care about my research anymore, even though I’m so close. Starting tasks feels impossible. I keep thinking I’m a failure, that I’ve wasted my life. Sometimes I even imagine stepping in front of a train near the station when I walk to campus—it’s specific, like I’ve pictured the timing, the noise… how no one would stop it.

But there are other things, too. I keep seeing my advisor in my peripheral vision, standing in doorways or outside my apartment, though when I turn, he’s not there. And I know—deep down—that he must be in love with me. He gives me these meaningful looks during meetings, subtle smiles… signs only I could understand. When I tried to ask him about it, he seemed confused, so I stopped talking to most people. Why bother?

I don’t go out. Conversations go off track—I start answering questions with something else entirely, I realize later. And sometimes, when my roommate jokes and moves my arm, it just… stays. Like wax. But I’m not sure if that matters. Nothing does.

I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—things at the lab are falling apart, and I can’t focus on my thesis. I keep seeing my advisor, Dr. Lang, standing in the hallway watching me, even when he’s not there. Sometimes he smiles, other times he mouths words I can't hear. I know he probably doesn’t realize how deeply he feels about me—we haven’t spoken much, but I’m certain there’s a connection. His presence lingers, like he’s trying to protect me.

My thoughts keep drifting during meetings. I start answering a question but end up talking about satellites or ocean tides—my committee notices, and I can see their confusion. I don’t even want to try anymore. I feel useless, like I’m a burden. Some mornings, I lie in bed for hours, not speaking, barely moving. I’ve thought about ending it—figured out how, when, even where I’d do it.

But here’s the thing—not everything lines up with the sadness. There were two weeks last month when I actually felt a bit better, more energy, less hopeless… and yet I still saw Dr. Lang in the library, still felt his affection, still had trouble staying on topic. The visions and the belief didn’t go away, even when the depression lifted slightly. That’s what makes me think it’s not just the depression talking.

Speaking takes so much effort now—I start a sentence and then trail off because nothing feels worth saying.

But there’s more—things I’m afraid to admit. I keep seeing my professor standing in the corner of my room at night, just watching. He’s never actually there when I turn on the light. And even though he doesn’t know I exist, I’m certain he’s in love with me. He sends me secret signs in emails, winks during lectures… no, he doesn’t really do that, but I *know* it’s true. I told a classmate once, and she got uncomfortable—so I stopped talking to anyone.

Sometimes when the nurse tried to examine me, my arm stayed bent where she placed it, like it was stuck in wax. I didn’t mean to do it—I just couldn’t bring myself to move. I’ve thought about how I’d do it—overdose on meds in my apartment when no one’s around. It feels like the only way out. But the visions and the beliefs—those only get worse when I’m this low. They’ve never happened when I wasn’t depressed.

D007-D015_h017.question_both:
I’ve been feeling awful for almost a year now—sad all the time, like a weight I can’t shake. I used to enjoy things, but now I don’t even want to get out of bed. I sleep 8 or 9 hours, but I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t sleep at all. I’m eating more than before—mindlessly snacking just to feel something—but I’m losing energy instead of gaining strength. My husband says I’ve become quiet, and he’s right. Some days, I just don’t have much to say. Words feel heavy.

For the past 8 months, I’ve also had these strange sensations—like bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night. No doctor’s found anything, but I *feel* it. And… I can’t help but think someone’s watching me. Not just once—constantly. I check the locks multiple times. I feel like my coworkers are in on something, whispering about me, or that my phone’s being monitored. I know it sounds extreme, but it feels real.

I can’t focus at work. I make mistakes now—things I never did before. I’m scared I’ll lose my job. I don’t know if the thoughts started with the sadness or came later. They’re just… both there, all the time.
D007-D015_h017.question_a:
I’ve been struggling for about ten months now—maybe a bit longer. I feel heavy all the time, like I’m moving through mud. I’m sad constantly, no matter what I do. I used to worry about my weight, but now I can’t stop eating—snacking all day, even when I’m not hungry. I sleep eight hours, but I wake up exhausted, like I never slept at all. I’m too tired to keep up with my caseload at work; I’ve made mistakes I never would’ve before, and my husband keeps telling me I’m pulling away, not talking like I used to.

For the past eight months, I’ve also felt like I’m being watched. Not just at home—everywhere. I think my insurance company put tracking devices in my phone and car. Sometimes at night, I feel bugs crawling under my skin, like something’s moving beneath it. I can’t explain it, but I *feel* it. I used to talk back, argue about it, but now I just don’t have the words. It’s easier to stay quiet.

The scary part? There were two weeks last month—clear as today—where I wasn’t sad at all. I still felt the crawling, still believed they were watching me, but the depression lifted. I didn’t cry, didn’t crave food. But the psychosis didn’t go away. It’s like parts of my mind aren’t connected.
D007-D015_h017.question_b:

My husband keeps telling me I’m eating more—especially sweets—and I haven’t cared about my weight lately.

The worst part started around eight months ago. I began feeling like someone was watching me, even at home. I’m convinced my neighbors are spying on me, maybe even putting something in the air vents. I’ve felt bugs crawling on my skin when there’s nothing there. I’ve stopped talking much because what’s the point? Words just feel heavy. But here’s the thing—none of these thoughts or sensations ever happened before I got so depressed. When I started feeling low, *then* the paranoia and the itching came. And they’ve never gone away completely since, but they’re always tied to how bad my mood is. When I feel worse, they get louder, stronger. They don’t exist on their own—they come with the sadness, not before or after.

Sometimes I feel hands on my arms when no one’s around, and it’s not comforting—it’s unsettling. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside me, like my organs are rotting or poisoning me, even though the doctors say my physicals are fine. I’ve told coworkers they should check, but they don’t understand.

I used to be sharp on calls, but now I can’t focus. My face probably doesn’t show much—I’ve been told I sound flat, like a robot. I don’t know how long this has been going on—months, maybe close to a year—but the strange sensations and thoughts… they’ve been there almost the whole time. I can’t tell when one starts and the other stops.
D007-D015_h018.question_a:

I lost over 15 pounds because I just… forgot to eat. I’d wake up at 3 a.m. every day, wide awake, heart racing, and just lie there, exhausted but unable to go back to sleep. The fatigue never goes away, no matter how much I rest.

But it’s not just the depression. For at least eight months, I’ve also felt like something’s wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting, even though every scan and test the docs ran came back normal. I can’t shake that feeling. And sometimes, I feel bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I *feel* it—hands on me, pulling at my flesh, even when I’m alone. My partner noticed I don’t talk much anymore, barely react, just stare.

Here’s the thing: even during brief times when I didn’t feel as down, those sensations and delusions stuck around. There was a two-week stretch last month—after a brief improvement in mood—where I still felt the bugs crawling and believed my liver was failing, even though I wasn’t depressed then.
